title: Log dualizing polarization and reconstruction of marked nodal families
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. A marked nodal family in this statement is a projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism $f:X\to S$ with nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], all of whose singularities are ordinary double points, together with finitely many pairwise disjoint sections $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ in its relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Here an ordinary double point has completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The integer $n$ may be zero. Write $D=\sum_i a_i(S)$ for the effective Cartier divisor of sections and $\mathcal O_X(D)$ for its associated invertible module [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. There is a canonical relative dualizing invertible module $\omega_{X/S}$ [def-sc-invertible-module], with the local complete-intersection adjunction normalization of [def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum]; its restriction to the relative smooth locus is $\Omega^1_{X/S}$, and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. Put $L=\omega_{X/S}\otimes\mathcal O_X(D)$. For each normalization $C$ of an irreducible component of a geometric fibre, $\deg(L|_C)=2g(C)-2+r_C$, where $r_C$ counts branches of nodes and markings on $C$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-genus, def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. If these numbers are positive for every such $C$, then $L$ is relatively ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: its restriction above each affine open of $S$ is ample. Whenever $L$ is relatively ample, the canonical evaluation map is an isomorphism $X\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Proj}_S(\bigoplus_{m\ge0}f_*L^{\otimes m})$ [def-nagata-relative-proj, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. In particular over $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ it identifies $X$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_{m\ge0}H^0(X,L^{\otimes m}))$ as an $R$-scheme, with the section-ring operations of [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. These canonical maps commute with isomorphisms of marked families. No smoothness of the generic fibre, normality or integrality of $S$, or morphism to another curve is assumed.

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness, hence separatedness and quasi-compactness. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-family-regular-affine-presentations] to the given flat finitely presented nodal family: over every base affine it supplies the regular curve presentations needed for adjunction.

proof.text: [lem-sfb-locnoeth-lci-curve-adjunction-gluing] applies to these presentations. It gives the canonical invertible $\omega$, the Jacobian-normalized fundamental class and Ext datum, the smooth-locus identification, and arbitrary-base-change and isomorphism comparisons.

source.place: Tags 0B6V (lemma-lci-shriek), 0E2Y (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing), 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci). Agent affine-refinement gluing formulation of former item steps 4--5, using the existing signed fundamental-class comparison; not a claim that 0E9Z verbatim treats nonproper morphisms.

proof.text: Use this $\omega$ as the supplied $K$ in [lem-sfb-smooth-marking-normalization-twist]. Its fibre identifications are those of step 2. This gives the relative Cartier divisor $D$, the invertible twist $L$, and $\deg(\nu^*L)=2g(C)-2+\#B_C+\#M_C=2g(C)-2+r_C$, including empty markings and self-nodes.

source.place: Tags 0C1A (lemma-genus-smooth), 0BS6 (lemma-rr), and divisors.tex Tag 067R (lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion). Agent marked-twist assembly of former item steps 6--9, using lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction for the ambient-branch comparison (Temkin, Stable modification of relative curves, section 1.2(b)); its source PDF is wanted, not claimed read.

proof.text: If these degrees are positive, [lem-trf-fibre-degree-ample-criterion] makes $L$ ample on each geometric fibre, which is proper over its field by clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] for the proper $f$. The ampleness descent clause of [lem-pc-very-ample-descends] gives ampleness on each ordinary fibre, which is proper by the same clause, hence of finite type, over its residue field. [lem-trf-ample-neighbourhood] gives relative ampleness near every base point. Refine by base affines and apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover], using quasi-compactness of $f$, to obtain ampleness above every affine open of $S$.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y (lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components); more-morphisms.tex Tag 0D2S (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood). Former item step 10.

proof.text: Whenever $L$ is relatively ample, apply [lem-sfb-proper-ample-section-proj-reconstruction] to the proper $f$ and this invertible $L$. Its canonical evaluation isomorphism and affine-base section-ring description give both reconstruction assertions.

source.place: Tags 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample) and 0C6J (lemma-proper-ample-is-proj); constructions.tex Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj) for the graded-isomorphism chart formula. Agent formulation with naturality, extracting former item steps 11--14.

proof.text: An isomorphism of marked families preserves $\omega$ with its adjunction comparisons by step 2, and preserves its marked twist by step 3. Apply the polarized naturality equality of [lem-sfb-proper-ample-section-proj-reconstruction] to the resulting $h^*L\simeq L\prime$. This makes the reconstruction square commute, compatibly with identities and composition.
